subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: NOTE 1 item 3 - an EAE's result is implementor-defined if one or more of the arithmetic expressions that COMPOSE it produces implementor-defined results (--check 15.4.1 'produces implementor-defined results' -> OK at Sec.15.4.1 rule 3; the standard-mode twin at rule 2 b) reads 'produce', the singular/plural verb being the only textual difference, and both were checked so this row does not rest on the sibling's number). The composing expression this compiler meets is exponentiation with a non-integer exponent, which Sec.8.8.1.5.4 r2 e) makes implementor-defined. TWO HALVES ARE OWED AND BOTH ARE NOW MET. HALF ONE - the function arm and the `**` arm converge on ONE result: IntrinsicRenderer's standard-mode arm renders FUNCTION EXP as DecPow(DecE, DecArg(ic,0), IntermediateMode) and FUNCTION EXP10 as DecPow(DecFrom('10','0'), ...), while NumericRenderer.Power emits DecPow(DecOperand(b), DecOperand(e), IntermediateMode) under the same predicate - the same runtime entry, the same operand conversion, the same rounding mode. That half was upheld when this row was REFUTED to PARTIAL. HALF TWO - THE REFUTATION'S HALF, AND IT IS WHAT CHANGED. The refutation read: 'CobolDec.cs#Pow, non-integer-exponent branch (line 139): return FromDouble(Math.Pow(b.ToDouble(), e.ToDouble())) - both operands leave SDIDI form for binary64 before the development begins, and the development is IEEE binary64 (~17 significant digits, base 2), not the decimal128 operations Sec.8.8.1.5.3 names. So the composing expression's implementor-defined result is developed OUTSIDE the latitude this row's CONFORMS rests on.' That line no longer exists. Owner decision D-C (2026-08-30; kb/Work PB167) replaced it with ONE development carried entirely on CobolDec Add/Sub/Mul/Div - operands never leave SDIDI form and every add/sub/mul/div is a Sec.8.8.1.5.3 decimal operation - and CobolDecPowDevelopmentTests fails if any binary64 transcendental is spelled in the file. The wave that landed D-C also carried two defects of its own into this arm, both fixed before this row was re-verdicted: kb/Work PB266 (r3's reciprocal was spelled in two arms of four, so a negative non-integer exponent did not evaluate the expression r3 mandates) and kb/Work PB267 (the past-loop-bound escape rebuilt the exponent from a CLAMPED long, so an exponent past 2**63-1 was silently replaced). PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-08-31. CLOSING TEST, and it answers the refutation's own objection ('No leg asserts FUNCTION EXP10(0.5) = 10 ** 0.5'): conformance:cases/8.8.1.5.4-Exponentiation-in-standard-decimal-arithmetic/pb167_sdidi_exponentiation now carries that leg directly, beside EXP10(0.5) = FUNCTION SQRT(10) and 10 ** 0.5 = FUNCTION SQRT(10) - so the function, the spelled-out EAE and the value Sec.15.84.4 r2 fixes exactly are pinned as one value rather than pairwise. conformance:cases/8.8.1.5.4-Exponentiation-in-standard-decimal-arithmetic/exp_standard_decimal_eae keeps the same-for-all-instances legs (P09/P17, rebaselined by D-C from the binary64 ...950 to the spec-exact ...933). BOUNDARY KEPT: the STANDARD-DEVIATION defect on RV-15.4.1-L2.1/-L2.2 is NOT an instance of this item - Sec.15.86.4 r1 composes its EAE from FUNCTION SQRT, whose standard-decimal value Sec.15.84.4 r2 specifies exactly, so no composing expression there produces an implementor-defined result. EDITIONS: batch default; NOTE 1's list makes items 2-4 mode-neutral.
